researched_by: the council's own car park order articles and schedule, its PSPO papers, its car park pages, and three years of Keswick Reminder reporting
policy_summary:
No designated overnight motorhome provision anywhere in Cumberland. There is no motorhome page, no aire, no overnight bay, and no scheme under consideration by the council itself. What there is instead is a blanket sleeping ban buried in car park orders the council inherited and never rewrote.

THE LEGACY ORDERS STILL APPLY. Cumberland was created in April 2023 from Allerdale, Carlisle and Copeland, and three years on the parking regime is still three regimes. The operative instrument in the west and north-west is the ALLERDALE BOROUGH COUNCIL (OFF-STREET PARKING PLACES) ORDER 2018, which commenced on 28 May 2019 and which Cumberland was still amending under its old name in September 2025. Its Article 31 is unambiguous: 'No person shall use any part of a Car Park or any Motor Vehicle parked in a Parking Space:- a) for sleeping or camping or cooking'. That single clause covers every council car park in Workington, Cockermouth, KESWICK, Wigton, Maryport and ALLONBY. In Carlisle the equivalent is paragraph 17 of the City of Carlisle off-street order, which prohibits use for sleeping, camping, eating or cooking. The Copeland order - Whitehaven, Egremont, ST BEES, Millom, Cleator Moor - could not be located online at all.

The schedule matters as much as the articles. Every car park in the Allerdale order permits only 'Motor cars, motorcycles and Heavy Motor Cars not exceeding 3.5 tonnes'. Anything over 3.5t is outside the permitted class in every former-Allerdale car park, which rules out most coachbuilts and every A-class. Maximum stays are set per site and range from 2 hours to 120 hours; the four ALLONBY seafront car parks are capped at 8 HOURS, which makes overnight parking there impossible before you even reach the sleeping ban.

THE KESWICK CONTRADICTION. Lakeside long stay car park sells an overnight ticket - 7pm to 7am for GBP1.10 - while its signage prohibits overnight occupancy and Article 31 prohibits sleeping. The council takes your money for the hours you are not allowed to be there. Keswick Town Council has been raising this since 2023; on peak weekends 50-plus campervans have used the car park, with chemical toilet waste dumped in Cockshot Wood, at Crosthwaite church and at the rugby club. Through 2024 and most of 2025 enforcement was effectively nil. That has changed: van users report signage everywhere from spring 2025 and a warden photographing vehicles and issuing penalties in June 2026.

Separately, the CUMBERLAND COUNCIL PUBLIC SPACES PROTECTION ORDER (NO. 1) 2024 came into force in November 2024 for three years, consolidating the three districts' PSPOs. It prohibits camping or sleeping overnight 'with or without a tent, inclusive of the activity referred to as Wild Camping' where the behaviour causes or attracts anti-social behaviour. The press reported it as a fly-camping crackdown in the Lake District, Wasdale named. It does not mention vehicles.
notes:
The direction of travel is one-way tightening, and it is being done without anyone deciding anything. Cumberland has not made a motorhome policy; it has simply carried forward three district orders that already banned sleeping, and then started enforcing one of them. There is no report to executive, no consultation, no press release. The whole regime is a 2018 Allerdale clause plus a 2026 warden with a camera.

The Keswick tariff is the sharpest thing in this file. Selling a GBP1.10 overnight ticket on a car park where sleeping is an offence is not an oversight anyone has been willing to fix, because the alternative - conceding that a paid overnight ticket implies permission to be there - is exactly the argument van users make. Keswick Town Council's clerk reported contacting Cumberland officers and getting no reply.

The only expansionary signal in the whole authority comes from a TOWN council, not this one. Keswick Town Council has been trying to get an aire since February 2023 (Crosthwaite Road car park was floated, four to five vans, objected to on hospital-proximity grounds) and by February 2026 was pushing a joint campervan strategy with the Lake District National Park Authority. Cumberland's role in that is enforcement, not provision. Note the shape: the body that wants provision has no car parks, and the body with the car parks wants enforcement.

The 3.5 tonne class limit is worth reading across the dataset. Westmorland and Furness applies the same figure at Penrith. That is both halves of the old Cumbria excluding the same vehicles by the same threshold, arrived at independently through inherited district orders.

Whitehaven's harbourside car parks are NOT the council's - Quay Street North and South, Tangier Street and Queens Dock belong to Whitehaven Harbour Commissioners, and three of the four carry a 2.2m height barrier, which settles the question for vans regardless of policy. Do not attribute those to Cumberland.

And Silloth, flagged as a pressure point, turns out to be largely outside Cumberland's parking estate: the town's car parks are run by Silloth-on-Solway Town Council and no Silloth site appears in the Allerdale order schedule. That is a gap in this record, not a finding of no restriction.
open_questions: The Copeland off-street parking order could not be found online in any form. Whitehaven, Egremont, St Bees, Millom and Cleator Moor car parks are therefore recorded with an unverified instrument. Does it carry an Article 31 equivalent, and does it impose the same 3.5t class limit?
Silloth's car parks appear to belong to Silloth-on-Solway Town Council, whose website returned 401. What are the rules there, and does Cumberland have any Silloth car park at all?
Is Lakeside Keswick's GBP1.10 overnight tariff still being sold in 2026 now that enforcement has started? If so the contradiction is live and a van user has a genuine argument.

What is the actual penalty for sleeping in a car park - a PCN under the parking order (GBP70/GBP50 tiers), or a PSPO fixed penalty? Van users report a figure of GBP60 per person per night at Keswick, which matches neither.

Does the Cumberland PSPO (No. 1) 2024 camping clause reach people sleeping in vehicles, or only tents? The drafting says 'with or without a tent' but never says vehicle, and the council has not tested it.
The Keswick TRO review consulted May-June 2025. The proposals were not published on the consultation page - did any of them address overnight or campervan parking on Keswick streets?
Coordinates for the four Allonby seafront car parks could not be pinned individually from any source.

sites.name: Castle car park (Devonshire Walk), Carlisle
sites.search_hint: Castle car park, Devonshire Walk, Carlisle
sites.notes: The only Cumberland car park with bays designated for motor caravans: 16 spaces shared between coaches, caravans, minibuses, motor caravans and campers, alongside 321 general spaces. Charges apply 8.30am to 6pm only, GBP4.20 all day for those classes, so a vehicle already in a bay pays nothing overnight. The gates are locked from 8pm to 6.30am and there is a GBP45 out-of-hours release fee to leave early, which is why van users treat it as a de facto overnight stop. Paragraph 17 of the City of Carlisle off-street parking order nonetheless prohibits using a vehicle for sleeping, camping, eating or cooking. Recorded as provision because the bays are real and the overnight parking is lawful; the sleeping is not. Park4night reviewers report the gates are often left unlocked in practice, and that freight trains run through the night.

sites.name: Lakeside long stay car park, Keswick
sites.search_hint: Lakeside long stay car park, Keswick
sites.notes: THE CONTRADICTION SITE. The council sells a 7pm-7am overnight ticket for GBP1.10 while the signage prohibits overnight occupancy and Article 31 of the Allerdale 2018 order prohibits sleeping, camping or cooking. Maximum stay 24 hours; permitted classes are coaches plus motor cars, motorcycles and heavy motor cars not exceeding 3.5 tonnes. Fifty-plus campervans on peak weekends and bank holidays, with chemical toilet waste dumped in Cockshot Wood and at Crosthwaite church. Enforcement was effectively nil through 2024 and into 2025 - a town councillor asked for 'a couple of weekends blitzing and issuing penalty notices'. It has now arrived: van users report signs everywhere from spring 2025 and a warden photographing vehicles and issuing fines in June 2026. Treat this as enforced.
sites.geocode_precision: the lakeside car park off Lake Road at the Derwentwater landing stages

sites.name: Allonby seafront car parks (North, Central, South and Southern areas)
sites.search_hint: Allonby beach car parks, Allonby, Cumbria
sites.notes: Four car parks along the Allonby seafront, items 1.42 to 1.45 of the Allerdale 2018 order schedule, each capped at a MAXIMUM STAY OF 8 HOURS. That is the shortest cap on the Cumberland coast and it makes overnight parking impossible on its own terms, before Article 31's sleeping ban is reached. Permitted classes are motor cars, motorcycles and heavy motor cars not exceeding 3.5 tonnes. Cumberland resurfaced and regraded them in March and April 2025, so the estate is being maintained, not abandoned. Individual coordinates could not be pinned from any source; the car parks run along the B5300 through and just north of the village.
sites.geocode_precision: not pinned - four separate car parks along roughly 2km of the B5300 seafront

sites.name: St Bees Foreshore car park, St Bees
sites.search_hint: St Bees Foreshore car park, Beach Road, St Bees
sites.notes: The big Copeland-side coastal car park and the start of the Coast to Coast, so a natural overnight target. Maximum stay 12 hours at GBP8.80, with a seven-day permit at GBP33; charges apply 8am to 8pm; no height barrier. The 12-hour cap means overnight parking is outside the tariff even though the car park is open all day. The controlling instrument is the legacy Copeland off-street parking order, which could not be located in any public source - so whether it carries the Allerdale order's explicit sleeping and camping ban is UNVERIFIED. Confidence low deliberately: the restriction on stay length is documented, the sleeping position is not.
sites.geocode_precision: beachfront car park at the end of Beach Road

sites.name: All Cumberland car parks in the former Allerdale area
sites.notes: ALLERDALE BOROUGH COUNCIL (OFF-STREET PARKING PLACES) ORDER 2018, commenced 28 May 2019, still in force and still being varied by Cumberland Council under its old name as recently as September 2025. Article 31: 'No person shall use any part of a Car Park or any Motor Vehicle parked in a Parking Space:- a) for sleeping or camping or cooking'. Covers Workington, Cockermouth, Keswick, Wigton, Maryport, Allonby and Harrington - roughly fifty car parks. Every entry in the schedule limits permitted classes to 'Motor cars, motorcycles and Heavy Motor Cars not exceeding 3.5 tonnes', which puts larger motorhomes outside the permitted class entirely; a trailer must occupy no more than two spaces and pay separately. Maximum stays run from 2 hours to 120 hours depending on the site, so multi-day PARKING is lawful at several Keswick, Cockermouth and Workington long stays. Sleeping in the vehicle is not lawful at any of them.

sites.name: All Cumberland car parks in the former Carlisle area
sites.notes: The legacy City of Carlisle off-street parking places order remains the instrument for Carlisle's car parks - Bitts Park, Castle, Citadel, Caldew Riverside, Cecil Street, Lowther Street, Paddy's Market, Swifts Bank, The Sands, Viaduct, West Walls. Its paragraph 17 prohibits using a vehicle for sleeping, camping, eating or cooking - a wider list than Allerdale's, since it catches eating. Sourced from a motorhome forum thread quoting the paragraph rather than from the order itself, which sits behind a robots-blocked tribunal archive; hence medium confidence on the wording, high on the substance.

sites.name: All Cumberland car parks in the former Copeland area
sites.notes: Whitehaven, Egremont, St Bees, Millom, Haverigg, Cleator Moor and Eskdale. The legacy Copeland off-street parking order could not be found online in any form - not on cumberland.gov.uk, not on the archived copeland.gov.uk, not in the traffic penalty tribunal archive. Recorded so the gap is visible rather than silently absent. What IS documented is that the individual car park pages carry maximum stays (12 hours at St Bees) and no overnight tariff. Assume a sleeping prohibition by analogy with Allerdale and Carlisle, but do NOT state it as fact until the order is seen. Note also that Whitehaven's harbourside car parks belong to Whitehaven Harbour Commissioners, not the council, and mostly carry 2.2m height barriers.

sites.name: Cumberland Council Public Spaces Protection Order (No. 1) 2024 - camping and overnight sleeping
sites.notes: In force from November 2024 for three years, to November 2027, consolidating the PSPOs of Allerdale, Carlisle and Copeland after reorganisation. Consulted 18 March to 26 April 2024, approved by Executive 23 July 2024. The clause: 'No person shall camp or sleep overnight with or without a tent, inclusive of the activity referred to as Wild Camping' where their behaviour causes or attracts anti-social behaviour. Breach is a level 3 fine on summary conviction, with fixed penalty notices as the routine route. Schedule A covers town and city centres including Carlisle, Workington, Whitehaven, Keswick, Cockermouth and Maryport; the council also applies it across its Lake District land, and the press reported it specifically as a fly-camping crackdown with Wasdale named. IMPORTANT: the order never mentions vehicles, campervans or motorhomes. It is drafted around tents and rough sleeping and is conditional on anti-social behaviour, so it is not a clean overnight-vehicle ban. applies_to left unknown for that reason.
